analysis:
This PR changes only the CI threat-review tooling under .github/scripts/threat_review. It does not touch provider, coordinator, attestation, cache or billing code. None of the canonical provider threats apply directly: T-041, TB-002/007/009/011 and A-001..A-017 are unaffected.

bedrock.py (head 46-84): adds an opt-in BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY=workload.
- Under workload, the limit starts at 0 and grows via plan_calls() to planned+1, capped at a bounded ceiling (<=500).
- Exceeding the ceiling raises BudgetStopped and sets workload_stopped. The stopped property (line 88) then blocks later calls and the OpenRouter fallback.
- The fixed policy keeps the bounded 1-100 allowance.
- Output tokens default to 16384 under workload; this is still within the existing 256-16384 bound.
- Invalid count or policy values fail closed. Accounting, fallback and uncertain-outcome handling (lines 159-222) are unchanged in kind.

budget_scan.py: adds a finished flag in the snapshot, set after run(). It calls plan_calls before the source, depth and integration stages (head 303-305, 317-327, 332, 367). Only the native adapter has a planner; OpenRouter keeps its durable dollar limits.

budget_runner.py:
- Rejects GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT != 1 (head 175-177) inside the try block, so the failure is checkpointed and published as errors.
- Marks snapshot finished on exceptions (line 225).
- status_body (38-48) now emits a human-review-required banner for incomplete or failed scans. 'Scan completed.' is emitted only when complete. complete still requires integration, full coverage, no limited files, no errors and no pending depth.
- The force_deep permission check is unchanged.

No regression found: the changes tighten failure signalling and add bounded, fail-closed call admission. Cost is bounded by the ceiling.

Unverified (outside the supplied evidence):
- The workflow YAML: whether it sets the workload policy, removes dispatch, or whether the retry-reject affects required-check semantics.
- The merge-clearance consumer of the result file: does it rely on complete versus finished?
